findings.description: `createSaveAll.tap()` marks each PID handed as soon as `download(file)` returns, although `downloadFile` only clicks an anchor and receives no download outcome. When the browser blocks or denies successive automatic downloads, those files are excluded from later batches and the person is told there is nothing new to save.
findings.title: Blocked downloads disappear from Save all

citations.citation: Chrome documents a separate Automatic downloads permission for sites downloading related files together.

evidence.explanation: The download callback calls `a.click()` without receiving confirmation, but the batch immediately adds the PID to `handed`, which `saveBatch` excludes thereafter. Chrome exposes a site permission for downloading multiple related files, so the 400 ms spacing does not establish that each click was allowed.

findings.description: `save(p)` adds a photo to `saveAll.handed` only after its share promise resolves, while `createSaveAll.tap()` does not coordinate with individual saves. If someone taps a print and then Save all while the first share is pending, both paths can select the same file; a second share may also reject because another share is in progress.
findings.title: Concurrent saves can duplicate a photo

citations.citation: InvalidStateError can occur when another sharing operation is in progress.

evidence.explanation: The individual handler marks the PID only on fulfillment, whereas the batch excludes only PIDs already in `handed`; its `busy` guard applies only to batch taps. The browser documents rejection when another sharing operation is in progress.

findings.description: `createSaveAll.tap()` catches a thrown `download()` call with only `console.warn`, after announcing that the whole batch is downloading. If object-URL creation or the anchor click throws for one file, the batch continues without telling the person which file needs another tap.
findings.title: Failed batch downloads get no warning

evidence.explanation: The loop emits its toast before downloading, catches each exception without another toast, and marks only successful calls. The browser callback performs URL creation and anchor clicking, either of which can fail synchronously.

findings.description: `createSaveAll.tap()` sets `downloadNext` on a non-cancellation share error but never clears it after the next tap downloads the batch. A transient failure, including a concurrent-share rejection, therefore makes later Save all taps bypass an available share sheet for the rest of the tab session.
findings.title: One share failure disables future sharing

citations.citation: | F13 | Unit, System | `tests/saveall.test.mjs`: 12 received photos go to the share sheet in one call, made inside the tap. Own photos, thumbnails and prints never fetched are left out and full photos still arriving are counted. A batch the share sheet can't take, or no share sheet, downloads one at a time `DOWNLOAD_GAP` apart. A cancel does nothing. Another failure downloads nothing until the next tap, which downloads everything not yet handed over, then the share sheet is tried again. Nothing is handed over twice, and a tap during a download batch starts nothing. The two-browser test taps Save all on a laptop: all 5 received files download byte-identical, and a second tap downloads nothing (exists) |

evidence.explanation: The flag is initialized false, checked before `canShare`, and set true on failure; the download branch contains no reset. The added testing guidance explicitly says sharing is tried again after the fallback batch.

findings.description: `saveBatch` checks ownership and prior handoff but never checks whether a received file is a photo. Since the picker accepts videos and received videos enter the same `files` map, Save all also shares or downloads them despite the photo-only Save all requirement.
findings.title: Save all includes videos as well as photos

evidence.explanation: F13 specifies received photos, while the application accepts video files and stores received full files together. The new test explicitly expects an MP4 to appear in the batch.

findings.description: `createSaveAll.tap()` sets `busy` before awaiting `share(list)` and clears it only when that promise settles. If the browser leaves the promise pending, every subsequent Save all tap returns “Still saving,” with no way to retry from the page.
findings.title: A pending share locks Save all indefinitely

evidence.explanation: Every tap exits at the busy guard once `busy` is set; its only reset is in `finally`, after the awaited share finishes. The button handler supplies no other recovery path.

findings.description: `createSaveAll.tap()` treats fulfillment of `navigator.share()` as proof that every selected photo was handed over and adds all their PIDs to `handed`. On Windows the promise can resolve when the share popup opens, so dismissing that popup can leave every photo excluded from later Save all taps without a completed handoff.
findings.title: Cancelled Windows shares cannot be retried

citations.citation: On Windows the share promise resolves when the popup launches; on Android it resolves after data is passed to the target.

evidence.explanation: The batch unconditionally marks every PID after the share promise resolves, and subsequent selection excludes marked PIDs. MDN states that on Windows the promise resolves when the popup is launched, unlike Android where it resolves after data reaches the target.
